title: First Non-Repeating Letter in a Stream

concept.title: A queue of candidates and a table of counts
body: Letters arrive one at a time. After each letter you want the **first letter that has appeared only once so far**. Keep two things: a table `count` with how often each letter occurred, and a **queue of candidates** in the order of their first arrival.

Letters that appeared twice are removed from the front, but only **when they reach the front**. That is enough: the answer only ever looks at the front. Every letter is queued at most once and removed at most once, so the total work is linear.

statement: Letters arrive one after another. After each letter print the first letter (in order of arrival) that has appeared exactly once so far, or `#` if there is none. Print the `n` answers as one word.
inputFormat: A single word of lowercase letters.
outputFormat: Print a word of the same length with the answer after each letter.

examples.note: After a: a. After aa: #. After aab: b. After aabc: b. The answer is a#bb.

hints: Count how often every letter appeared.
Keep a queue of letters that appeared once, in the order of arrival.
Remove letters from the front while their count is more than one; the front is the answer.

explanation: The queue lists the letters seen once, oldest first. Letters whose count grew are dropped when they reach the front, so the front is always the first non-repeating letter.
